newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND APPROVES PARTIAL SELL-OFF OF TPSA TELECOM.
newsitem.headline: POLAND APPROVES PARTIAL SELL-OFF OF TPSA TELECOM.

text.p: The Polish government approved on Tuesday a plan to float up to 25 percent of the state telecommunications monopoly TPSA in 1998 on Polish and international markets, the telecommunications minister said.

"Our concept is that the sale of TPSA (Telekomunikacja Polska SA) will start in 1998 and the government's decision today brings to a close a key stage of discussions and we are...entering the implementation stage," Andrzej Zielinski told a news conference.

Zielinski said the government plan assumed that the TPSA, Poland biggest state firm, would be privatised in stages with the first next year envisaging a public offering for both institutional and retail investors in Poland and abroad.

Zielinski said that after the first stage the state treasury would retain control over the company with up to 15 percent of TPSA shares set aside for its employees and the public offer capped at 25 percent.
He did not rule out that the offer of existing shares could be combined with a capital increase but did not give any details.
Zielinski said the government had yet to decide the exact size of the public offer and how the shares would be divided between the domestic and foreign tranches.

He also said the second stage of privatisation might involve finding a strategic investor but final decisions would be made by the cabinet in cooperation with a privatisation adviser Poland has yet to appoint.
"All details will be determined by the government together with privatisation adviser...who will evaluate the company and propose a (sell off) plan," Zielinski said.
